title: break: Exiting a Loop Early
learningObjectives: Explain break: exiting a loop early and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: break exits the nearest enclosing loop immediately and continues after it. In nested loops it does not automatically exit outer loops.
understand.whyItMatters: Searches can stop as soon as a match is found, avoiding unnecessary checks.
understand.explain: Use break with a clear exit condition; use a flag or helper function for multi-loop exit intent.

examples.title: Search and flag
examples.explanation: Flag stores whether a match was found.

examples.title: Inner loop break
examples.explanation: Break exits inner loop only; outer continues.

examples.title: Stop when sum reaches target
examples.explanation: Accumulation stops after reaching the threshold.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five break: Exiting a Loop Early examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating break: exiting a loop early in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: State exactly what condition triggers break.
Remember only the nearest loop is exited.
Use flags for result state if needed.

questions.explanation: break exits the nearest loop immediately.
